questions.q: An aircraft lands at an aerodrome (elevation 540 ft, QNH 993 hPa) with 1013 hPa still set. The altimeter reads about:
questions.e: Setting 1013 instead of 993 adds 20 hPa × 27 ft = 540 ft to the reading: 540 + 540 = 1,080 ft.

questions.q: An aircraft is at FL80 and the local QNH is 1000 hPa. With QNH set on the second altimeter, it will read about:
questions.e: QNH is 13 hPa below 1013, so the altitude is about 13 × 27 = 350 ft below the flight level: 8,000 − 350 ≈ 7,650 ft.

questions.q: Flying at FL100 between two coastal airports that both report QNH 1016 hPa, your true altitude decreases steadily. The most likely reason is:
o: The air at the destination is colder than at departure
One of the QNH values must be wrong
The air at the destination is warmer than at departure
questions.e: With equal QNH, the only thing changing the true altitude of a pressure level is temperature. Colder air lowers it.

questions.q: On a very cold winter day with regional QNH 1013 hPa set, you circle a mountain at exactly its summit height. Your altimeter will show:
o: A higher altitude than the summit elevation
The same altitude as the summit
A lower altitude than the summit
questions.e: In cold air the altimeter over-reads, so at the true summit height it shows more than the summit elevation. Dangerous for terrain clearance.

questions.q: The average height of the tropopause at about 50°N is approximately:
questions.e: Mid-latitudes are close to the ISA average of 11 km (36,090 ft). Polar values are about 8 km and equatorial about 16 km.

o: Subsidence through most of the troposphere
questions.e: The turrets show convection starting at middle levels, often a warning of later thunderstorms.

questions.q: In which cloud can airframe icing be virtually ruled out?
questions.e: Cirrus is made of ice crystals, which don't stick to the airframe.

questions.q: In a cumulonimbus, the heaviest ice accretion usually occurs between:
questions.e: That band holds the most large supercooled droplets.

in air colder than ISA the altimeter over-reads. Hot to cold, look out below.
correct by 4 ft per 1,000 ft per 1°C ISA deviation. Add if warmer, subtract if colder.
